packs.title: Visitor records and public park pages
packs.promise: Read admitted visitor settings, collect garden and farm arrangements, and make original records from actual park paths.

q.s: Collect relationships among a visitor route, structures and the garden edge.
st: Enter the opened admitted garden and stay on its ordinary visitor paths. Choose a comfortable short section without stepping into plantings or requiring a closed structure.

Collect three actual connections: where a path changes direction, where a structure meets or frames the route, and where a planted or water edge changes the view. Substitute another observed connection if one type is unavailable.
For each, write the two connected elements and the position from which you observed them. Describe visible form without assigning cultural symbolism or copying a visitor-map graphic.
Compare which connection makes this garden’s route most recognizable to you. Keep all marks on your own notes and make them after exit if needed.

q.s: Make an original page from the relationship between a park path and its lake.
st: Choose an opened dry public path position beside the lake and leave room for shared movement. Keep the shoreline and water outside the activity.
Write two actual relationships between path, lake edge and the wider park setting. Record a material, direction or distance relationship you can observe without moving off the path.

Create a personal one-page layout with an opening sentence, a central comparison and a closing question. A written layout works equally to a sketch; keep any imagined scene clearly marked as your idea.
Revise one line so it names a detail from this actual Doling view. Add a short note separating what you observed from what you imagined.

q.t: A western park path and return
q.s: Retrace a short asphalt segment away from the Art Museum construction.
st: Reach the opened western asphalt path and choose the short southward segment only if it is lawful and comfortable that day. Identify an existing path-edge feature as your start without leaving the pavement or moving anything. Leave construction, creek and museum access outside the route.

Use a watch or phone to time up to three minutes walking calmly south along that same asphalt path. Notice two actual changes in the surrounding tree spacing or path edge. Turn when three minutes have elapsed, or sooner before any junction, surface change, barrier or uncomfortable section.
Retrace the same segment to your chosen starting feature. Keep the task bounded rather than following the wider track or a greenway extension.
Write a completed-return note and compare the two outward observations with the return view. Include any current barrier or reason you would choose a different day.

packs.title: Two downtown afternoons
packs.promise: Connect opened visitor exhibits with distinct public frontages, then finish a short upper-park return.

q.t: Three records from an event building
q.s: Read a convention building from its public street frontage.
st: Reach an opened public sidewalk position along the actual Expo Center’s south-facing frontage. Keep queues, doors and loading areas clear.

Collect three visible building/frontage relationships: one change in the wall plane, one relationship between an entrance zone and public pavement, and one repeated exterior form. Use another observed relationship if a type is screened.
For each, name its position and describe what you can see without inferring an event schedule, interior arrangement or accessibility rating.
Add a short comparison of how this event building meets the street. Use the exact Expo identity rather than borrowing the nearby park or hotel address.

q.s: Make a personal postcard from a documented change of use.
st: Find an opened public south-side Walnut angle facing the historic main building’s south facade. Keep shared sidewalk and actual entries clear.
Write two actual exterior details, then paraphrase the operator’s temple-to-hotel history. Do not infer a former ritual or current guest experience from appearance.
Create a personal postcard with three parts: an observed facade detail, the sourced change of use, and a question you would leave for a later visit. A fully written layout works equally to drawing.
Revise one line so it clearly separates observation, documented history and your own response. Address it to an imagined recipient without sending it or speaking for the hotel.

q.t: A quarry park path and return
q.s: Retrace an upper park path without descending into the amphitheater.
st: Reach the opened upper west-side public path and check that its short northern-bend segment is lawful and comfortable. Leave amphitheater steps, closed events and displays outside the activity.
Walk calmly along that upper path to its small northern bend. Notice two actual relationships between the dry path, planted edge and quarry-themed park layout without leaving the route.
Turn at the bend and retrace the same public segment to your start. Do not add the lower amphitheater or a wider downtown loop to the completion record.
Write a completed-return note, two path/layout observations and one comparison between outward and return views. Finish here with onward travel arranged separately.
